title: USB CDC: Add follow USB CDC Data stream
description:
Handle unknown traffic in USB CDC dissector to support follow stream. Follow CDC Data stream is especially useful for analyzing plain serial data that is commonly transmitted on "virtual COM" CDC ACM interface. Solve the IN and OUT endpoint bounding problem by generating stream index for each CDC interface that gets actual data traffic.

USBLL: Call USB dissector after USBLL address is set

Updating packet info with USBLL address after USB dissector set its own address breaks follow USB CDC stream functionality. Make reassembly the very last step to prevent address mismatches inside layers.

USB: Differentiate IN and OUT endpoints

All USB endpoints have assigned a number from 0 to 15. Default control endpoint is always endpoint 0 and it is virtually only control type endpoint (specification allows other control endpoints but there is really no point in doing so). Only control endpoints are bidirectional. Bulk, interrupt and isochronous endpoints are unidirectional.

Commonly used approach is to refer to IN endpoints the same way as these appear in endpoint descriptor bEndpointAddress field, i.e. with 0x80 direction bit set. Under this convention OUT endpoints are 0x01 - 0x0F and IN endpoints are 0x81 - 0x8F. It is important to note that IN endpoint 1 (0x81) is different endpoint from OUT endpoint 1 (0x01) despite both having endpoint address 1. It is possible for IN and OUT endpoint with the same endpoint number to be of different transfer type and even to belong to different interface.

Modify USB dissector to differentiate between the IN and OUT endpoints sharing the same endpoint numbers to correctly match the endpoints against interfaces if such endpoints happen to belong to different interfaces. Limit the change only to under the hood processing by clearing away the direction bit in USB address conversion function.
